ABOUT THE ATLAS

A map, not a single family tree.

AI techniques overlap. A single system can combine a neural architecture, several learning signals, external knowledge and a planning controller. This atlas separates those complementary facets so you can see how the pieces fit.

The classification and evolution figures are original to AI Atlas. They show complementary facets and selected influences, not exclusive ancestry. Figure views and topic guides are generated from shared source data.

The beginner introductions lead with concrete examples and uses. A shared six-term glossary is available beside each introduction. Read the plain-language review response and estimated readability comparison. Readability scores do not establish comprehension.

No institutional affiliation or endorsement is claimed. This is a versioned research snapshot, not an automatically updated feed or a comprehensive expert review. Read the changelog and review response.

References, with evidence

Each reference shows the latest recorded HTTP availability result. A successful response does not establish that a paper supports a claim. Restricted, rate-limited and failed network requests remain inconclusive.

Download the complete HTTP audit. The project includes the checker so these results can be reproduced with a new timestamp.

Use and attribution

Licensing and third-party notices. Referenced papers remain with their authors and publishers.

Your bookmarks and reading progress stay in this browser. Fonts are served with the application; this app makes no Google Fonts requests and includes no analytics. Opening a reference visits the external source.
